clue.text: I, among most at work, will be a committed union member

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being shifted about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says that, put among a busy workforce, they will be a loyal trade-union member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union member' looks like trade-union talk, but the union is a marriage. 'at work' rearranges I, AMONG and MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A monogamist keeps to one spouse, so they are a faithful member of a marriage.

clue.text: Doctor, calculating type, around one part of year

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go around the letter for one, holding it inside

parts.note: MD is short for Doctor of Medicine
I is the Roman numeral for one
a summer is someone who sums, a person doing calculations

explanation.surface: A medical man who is good with numbers hangs about for part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMER here is 'one who sums', not the season, even though the answer is a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer is the period around the June solstice, a portion of the calendar.

clue.text: Unpleasant films: one held up places of debauchery

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the indefinite article meaning one
a sty is a figurative den of filth and depravity

explanation.surface: Nasty films: someone was robbed in seedy dens of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: Video nasties was the 1980s British tabloid term for violent horror films on video.
explanation.definitionFit: Video nasties were gory or violent horror videos, popularly just called nasties.

clue.text: Quantity of wine? Chat with son involves litre

indicators.note: the letters from chat and son take in the litre letter, holding it inside

parts.note: gas is informal for idle talk
L is the symbol for litre
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Chatting with your son over a litre of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass is a serving measure of wine; the question mark admits it is one example of a quantity.

clue.text: Demonstration about court case kept short for senior woman

indicators.note: the march letters go around the shortened trial

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: the trial is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

explanation.surface: A protest over a court case cut short, organised for an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' reads as a show of evidence in court, but here it is a protest walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the elderly female head of a family or group.

clue.text: Pace and power in germ

indicators.note: the power letter sits inside the word for germ

parts.note: a seed is the germ from which something grows
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Speed and strength are present in a germ, as if microbes were athletic.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace and speed are synonyms for rate of movement.

clue.text: One behaving contemptibly towards a daughter

parts.note: to means towards
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone acts despicably towards a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a toad is an idiom for a loathsome, contemptible person.

clue.text: Collected edition upset second writer (American)

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: mo is informal for a moment or second
a nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for the writer

explanation.surface: A collected edition upset a second author from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion but turns MO upwards to give OM.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a volume gathering several works by one author into one book.

clue.text: Medic, year upon year, accepting student in formal style

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: the two year letters take the student letter between them

parts.note: Y again for year
L is the learner plate letter, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A doctor, year after year, takes on a student with a stiff manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryly describes a restrained, unemotional, rather stiff manner of speaking or acting.

clue.text: Demolish inlet's dam after storm

indicators.note: after a storm things are scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A storm-damaged dam on an inlet must be pulled down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart or pull down a structure piece by piece.

clue.text: Cry of joy, embracing willing lover

indicators.note: the cry wraps around the word for willing

parts.note: hey is an exclamation of delight
on means willing, as in 'I'm on for that'

explanation.surface: A joyful shout as someone hugs an eager sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is an endearment used for a sweetheart, so it can stand for a lover.

clue.text: Mostly keep quiet in depression

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for keep is used

parts.note: to keep is to hold
low means quiet, as in a low voice

explanation.surface: Advice to keep mostly silent when you are feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood, but it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a small sunken area, a depression in a surface.

clue.text: Platoons, say, some of best in USA, retreating

indicators.note: retreating means the extracted run is read backwards
only part of the words best in USA is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some of America's finest military platoons are falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is one example of a military unit, as the 'say' signals.

clue.text: Independent? Independent participating in belly dancing, unforgettably

indicators.note: the second independent letter takes part inside the rearranged belly
dancing jiggles the letters of belly into a new order

explanation.surface: A free spirit taking part in belly dancing that will live long in the memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'Independent' is used twice in two different abbreviated forms, one three letters long and one a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelibly means in a way that cannot be erased, so something is never forgotten.

clue.text: Obscurity not observed in radio broadcast

indicators.note: a radio broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word for not observed is taken by its sound

parts.note: something missed was not noticed

explanation.surface: Something obscure went unnoticed on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is haze that obscures vision, a literal kind of obscurity.

clue.text: Refined sources of metal extremely well!

parts.note: gracious means elegant and refined

indicators.note: the sources of words are their first letters, here of metal and extremely

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising fine-quality metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well!' is an exclamation of surprise, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracious me is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: State idea on reforming Scotland as before

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: reforming reshapes the letters of idea and on into a new order

explanation.surface: A US state proposes reforming Scotland as it used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, now used poetically or historically.

clue.text: Still getting plea for help about new Government services

parts.note: even works as still, as in 'even better' = 'still better'

indicators.note: the distress signal goes around the letters for new and government

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: Government services still get an urgent appeal about something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' suggests public services, but they are church services; SOS wraps around N and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so evensongs are church services.

clue.text: One Judge probing journalist's criminal act

indicators.note: the one and judge letters push inside the journalist's word

parts.note: hack is informal for a journalist; the 's means 'journalist is'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge investigating a reporter's crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize a vehicle illegally, an act of crime.

clue.text: Chatter linked to predicament with target of pest control?

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for talking at length
being in a hole means being in a fix

explanation.surface: Gossip about someone's awkward situation and a pest-control job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit on' is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit burrows are blocked or gassed by those controlling the pest, so the hole is what they aim at.

clue.text: Fail quickly, overlooking original grandiloquence

parts.note: to bomb is to fail badly

indicators.note: the original, or first, letter is overlooked, so it is dropped

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A show that flops quickly and ignores originality is all hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated language with little substance.

clue.text: Run one?

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
an ace is a one on dice or cards

explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue invites you to run one; the parts are R for run and ACE for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest that competitors run, so it is something one may run.

clue.text: Account about one pub that's served up American coffee

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A report about a pub that serves American coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal gives RABICA; A for American goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the widely grown Coffea arabica plant and the beans it yields.

clue.text: Very busy, but ready to dispatch preserved goods?

parts.note: jam is fruit preserved with sugar
goods that are packed are ready to send out

explanation.surface: Busy times, but the jars of preserves are boxed and ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Jam-packed means crammed full, as a very busy place is.

clue.text: Biblical character penning a chapter identifying Biblical character

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so Job's letters go around the others

parts.note: Job is the long-suffering hero of the Book of Job

explanation.surface: One Bible figure writes a chapter naming another Bible figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is the Old Testament patriarch, son of Isaac, also called Israel.

clue.text: Gives up thrilling stimulants

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as in kicking a habit, means abandons it
second meaning: thrills, sources of excitement

explanation.surface: Someone quits taking exciting drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both abandoning a habit and the buzzes of excitement people seek.

clue.text: Fruit? Seems to have lost first two

indicators.note: the word for seems loses its opening two letters

parts.note: appears means seems

explanation.surface: A puzzled shopper notices two fruits seem to be missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pears are an orchard fruit; the question mark marks them as one example of the class.

clue.text: Running behind after pressure in horse race

indicators.note: after places the late letters following the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
running late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: A horse runs behind after being pressed in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a horse race with a prize, such as a trophy, for the winner.

clue.text: Sound of chains, cold and drooping

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
lank hair hangs limp and drooping

explanation.surface: A rattle of chains, chilly and sagging, like a dungeon scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A clank is the heavy metallic noise of chains knocking together.

clue.text: Transmissible disease? College head bearing identifying mark

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the head word holds the tag inside

parts.note: onion is old slang for the head
a tag is a label that identifies something

explanation.surface: A college principal wears a badge naming a contagious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College head' tempts you to take the first letter, but C is college and ONION is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Contagion is the passing of disease by contact, or the disease so spread.

clue.text: Possibly eighth in cricket team in English city

parts.note: everyone in a cricket team may be called on to bat, so a team member is a bat
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet, used to label the eighth item in a list

explanation.surface: A cricketer who may bat at number eight plays for a side in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one batting position, but 'Possibly eighth' gives H and 'in cricket team' gives BAT. Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is a historic spa city in the county of Somerset, famous for its Roman baths.

clue.text: Small group of people taken aback about country transport

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about the word for country, holding it inside
taken aback, read literally, means turned back to front, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a race is a group of people sharing descent
a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A small band of people is startled by some news about the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise, but read literally it means turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate cars are long-bodied family vehicles, the British term for station wagons, a means of getting about.
